jp: 彼[かれ]はかばんから財布[さいふ]を{取[と]り出[だ]した|cv-dasu}。
en: He took his wallet out of his bag.
why: 取り出す is to take something out of a container; the から shows where it comes out of.

jp: 子[こ]どもが急[きゅう]に道[みち]へ{飛[と]び出[だ]して|cv-dasu}、車[くるま]にひかれそうになった。
en: A child suddenly dashed out into the road and was nearly hit by a car.
why: 飛び出す means to rush or dash out; 飛び降りる is jumping down, 飛び上がる jumping up.

jp: 昔[むかし]の友達[ともだち]の名前[なまえ]をやっと{思[おも]い出[だ]した|cv-dasu}。
en: I finally remembered my old friend's name.
why: 思い出す is to recall a memory; 思い込む means to be convinced and 思い切る to resolve.

jp: 映画[えいが]が悲[かな]しくて、妹[いもうと]は突然[とつぜん]{泣[な]き出[だ]した|cv-dasu}。
en: The movie was so sad that my little sister suddenly burst into tears.
why: Verb stem + 出す marks a sudden start: 泣き出す is bursting into tears, not stopping or continuing.

jp: 信号[しんごう]が青[あお]になると、みんな一斉[いっせい]に{走[はし]り出[だ]した|cv-dasu}。
en: When the light turned green, everyone started running at once.
why: 走り出す is to break into a run; 走り切る means to run the whole distance, 走り回る to run around.

jp: 雨[あめ]が{降[ふ]り出[だ]した|cv-dasu}ので、すぐに傘[かさ]をさした。
en: It started to rain, so I put up my umbrella at once.
why: The umbrella goes up because the rain has just begun, so 降り出す (start falling) is needed.

jp: 授業[じゅぎょう]中[ちゅう]に、後[うし]ろの学生[がくせい]が突然[とつぜん]{笑[わら]い出[だ]した|cv-dasu}。
en: In the middle of class, the student behind me suddenly started laughing.
why: 笑い出す is to burst out laughing; the other verbs describe finishing, continuing or laughing something off.

jp: 会議[かいぎ]で部長[ぶちょう]が突然[とつぜん]新[あたら]しい計画[けいかく]を{言[い]い出[だ]した|cv-dasu}。
en: At the meeting the department head suddenly came out with a new plan.
why: 言い出す means to bring something up for the first time; 言い返す is to talk back and 言い直す to rephrase.

jp: 長[なが]い間[あいだ]止[と]まっていた工事[こうじ]が、ようやく{動[うご]き出[だ]した|cv-dasu}。
en: The construction that had been stopped for so long finally got moving.
why: After a long stop, 動き出す says that things have started to move.

jp: 猫[ねこ]がドアの隙間[すきま]から外[そと]へ{逃[に]げ出[だ]した|cv-dasu}。
en: The cat escaped outside through the gap in the door.
why: 逃げ出す is to get away out of somewhere; 逃げ込む would mean fleeing into a place, not out of it.

jp: 部屋[へや]に入[はい]ってきた犬[いぬ]を、母[はは]は庭[にわ]へ{追[お]い出[だ]した|cv-dasu}。
en: My mother chased the dog that had come into the room out into the garden.
why: 追い出す is to drive something out; 追い込む drives it in, and 追い越す means to overtake.

jp: 先生[せんせい]は問題[もんだい]を起[お]こした学生[がくせい]を研究室[けんきゅうしつ]に{呼[よ]び出[だ]した|cv-dasu}。
en: The teacher summoned the student who had caused trouble to the office.
why: 呼び出す is to call someone out and summon them; 呼び止める is calling out to stop someone.

jp: 銀行[ぎんこう]で十万[じゅうまん]円[えん]を{引[ひ]き出[だ]した|cv-dasu}。
en: I withdrew a hundred thousand yen at the bank.
why: 引き出す is to draw money out of an account; 引き受ける means to take on a job.

jp: 一時間[いちじかん]かかって、なくした鍵[かぎ]をやっと{探[さが]し出[だ]した|cv-dasu}。
en: After an hour I finally managed to find the key I had lost.
why: 探し出す means to search until you find; 探し回る only describes looking around, without the result.

jp: 音楽[おんがく]が始[はじ]まると、子[こ]どもたちは楽[たの]しそうに{踊[おど]り出[だ]した|cv-dasu}。
en: When the music began, the children happily started to dance.
why: The music has just begun, so the children started dancing: 踊り出す marks the beginning.

jp: 警察[けいさつ]は三日[みっか]かかって、ついに犯人[はんにん]を{見[み]つけ出[だ]した|cv-dasu}。
en: After three days the police finally tracked down the culprit.
why: 見つけ出す is to find something hidden or hard to find; 見落とす and 見逃す mean to miss it.

jp: 一歳[いっさい]になる前[まえ]に、あの子[こ]は{歩[ある]き出[だ]した|cv-dasu}。
en: That child started walking before turning one.
why: 歩き出す means to begin to walk; the other forms describe walking around, being tired or going on.

jp: 桜[さくら]がもう{咲[さ]き出[だ]した|cv-dasu}と、ニュースで言[い]っていた。
en: The news said the cherry blossoms have already started to bloom.
why: For the first blossoms, 咲き出す (begin to bloom) fits; 咲き誇る and 咲き乱れる describe full bloom.

jp: 怖[こわ]い映画[えいが]の途中[とちゅう]で、誰[だれ]かが{叫[さけ]び出[だ]した|cv-dasu}。
en: In the middle of the scary movie, someone suddenly started screaming.
why: 叫び出す is to start screaming suddenly; the others mean tired of, continuing or finishing screaming.

jp: 彼[かれ]はずっと黙[だま]っていたが、やがて静[しず]かに{話[はな]し出[だ]した|cv-dasu}。
en: He had been silent for a long time, but eventually he began to speak quietly.
why: After the silence the speech begins, so 話し出す (start talking) is right.

jp: 図書館[としょかん]の本[ほん]を外[そと]に{持[も]ち出[だ]して|cv-dasu}はいけません。
en: You must not take library books out of the building.
why: 持ち出す is to carry something out of a place; 持ち込む is the reverse, bringing it in.

jp: 先生[せんせい]が黒板[こくばん]に何[なに]か{書[か]き出[だ]した|cv-dasu}。
en: The teacher began to write something on the blackboard.
why: 書き出す here means to start writing; 書き終える is finishing and 書き直す is rewriting.

jp: 彼[かれ]は本[ほん]を手[て]に取[と]ると、夢中[むちゅう]で{読[よ]み出[だ]した|cv-dasu}。
en: As soon as he picked up the book, he started reading it eagerly.
why: He has just picked the book up, so 読み出す (begin reading) fits, not finishing or skipping.

jp: 乾杯[かんぱい]のあと、誰[だれ]かが大[おお]きな声[こえ]で{歌[うた]い出[だ]した|cv-dasu}。
en: After the toast, someone started singing loudly.
why: 歌い出す is to start singing; 歌い終える means to finish and 歌い続ける to keep going.

jp: 彼[かれ]の話[はなし]があまりに面白[おもしろ]くて、思[おも]わず{吹[ふ]き出[だ]した|cv-dasu}。
en: His story was so funny that I burst out laughing without meaning to.
why: 吹き出す is the set expression for bursting out laughing; the other verbs are about wind or blowing.

jp: 消防士[しょうぼうし]は燃[も]えている家[いえ]から子[こ]どもを{運[はこ]び出[だ]した|cv-dasu}。
en: The firefighter carried the child out of the burning house.
why: から marks the burning house as the place carried out of, so 運び出す is needed, not carrying in.

jp: 犬[いぬ]が急[きゅう]に大[おお]きな声[こえ]で{吠[ほ]え出[だ]した|cv-dasu}。
en: The dog suddenly started barking loudly.
why: 急に signals a sudden start, which is what 吠え出す (begin to bark) means.

jp: 気温[きおん]が上[あ]がって、川[かわ]の氷[こおり]が{溶[と]け出[だ]した|cv-dasu}。
en: The temperature rose and the ice on the river began to melt.
why: With rising temperature the ice begins to melt: 溶け出す marks the start of the process.

jp: その会社[かいしゃ]は来月[らいげつ]、新[あたら]しいスマートフォンを{売[う]り出[だ]す|cv-dasu}そうです。
en: I hear that the company will put a new smartphone on sale next month.
why: 売り出す means to put a product on the market for the first time; 売り払う is to sell off.

jp: 母[はは]は私[わたし]の話[はなし]を聞[き]いて、突然[とつぜん]{怒[おこ]り出[だ]した|cv-dasu}。
en: My mother suddenly got angry when she heard what I said.
why: 怒り出す is to suddenly become angry; the other verbs do not mean the anger starts.

jp: 地震[じしん]で、棚[たな]の上[うえ]の花瓶[かびん]が{揺[ゆ]れ出[だ]した|cv-dasu}。
en: In the earthquake, the vase on the shelf started to shake.
why: At the moment the quake hits, the vase begins to shake: 揺れ出す marks the start.

jp: 引[ひ]き出[だ]しからはさみを{取[と]り出[だ]して|cv-dasu}、紙[かみ]を切[き]った。
en: I took the scissors out of the drawer and cut the paper.
why: The scissors come out of the drawer, so 取り出す; 取り戻す is to get something back and 取り替える to swap.

jp: この歌[うた]を聞[き]くと、いつも子供[こども]の頃[ころ]を{思[おも]い出[だ]す|cv-dasu}。
en: Whenever I hear this song, I remember my childhood.
why: 思い出す is to call a past memory back to mind; 思い付く is to hit upon a new idea.

jp: 赤[あか]ちゃんは目[め]を覚[さ]ますと、すぐに{泣[な]き出[だ]した|cv-dasu}。
en: The baby woke up and started crying right away.
why: すぐに after waking points to a start, so 泣き出す (begin crying) is right.

jp: 駅[えき]に着[つ]くと、彼女[かのじょ]は改札[かいさつ]に向[む]かって{走[はし]り出[だ]した|cv-dasu}。
en: When she reached the station, she broke into a run toward the ticket gate.
why: She starts running toward the gate, so 走り出す; 走り切る means to finish a run.

jp: 彼[かれ]は怒[おこ]って、家[いえ]を{飛[と]び出[だ]して|cv-dasu}しまった。
en: He got angry and stormed out of the house.
why: Rushing out of a house in anger is 飛び出す; 飛び込む would mean jumping or rushing into it.

jp: 子[こ]どもたちは先生[せんせい]の変[へん]な顔[かお]を見[み]て、一斉[いっせい]に{笑[わら]い出[だ]した|cv-dasu}。
en: The children saw the teacher's funny face and all burst out laughing.
why: Seeing the face triggers sudden laughter, so 笑い出す; 笑い飛ばす is to laugh a problem off.

jp: 天気予報[てんきよほう]では晴[は]れだったのに、午後[ごご]から雪[ゆき]が{降[ふ]り出[だ]した|cv-dasu}。
en: The forecast said sunny, but in the afternoon it started to snow.
why: A change from a sunny forecast is the snow beginning, which is 降り出す.

jp: 弟[おとうと]が「学校[がっこう]を辞[や]めたい」と{言[い]い出[だ]して|cv-dasu}、家族[かぞく]みんなが驚[おどろ]いた。
en: My younger brother suddenly said he wanted to quit school, and the whole family was shocked.
why: 言い出す is to bring up a statement or idea for the first time, which is what surprised the family.

jp: 動物園[どうぶつえん]からサルが{逃[に]げ出[だ]した|cv-dasu}らしい。
en: Apparently a monkey has escaped from the zoo.
why: A monkey getting out of the zoo is 逃げ出す (break out and escape).

jp: 古[ふる]い写真[しゃしん]の中[なか]から祖母[そぼ]の顔[かお]を{探[さが]し出[だ]した|cv-dasu}。
en: I picked out my grandmother's face from among the old photographs.
why: Finding one face among many is 探し出す (search out), a result rather than just looking.

jp: 携帯[けいたい]電話[でんわ]で友達[ともだち]を公園[こうえん]に{呼[よ]び出[だ]した|cv-dasu}。
en: I phoned my friend and got them to come out to the park.
why: 呼び出す is to call someone out to a place; 呼び戻す is calling them back.

jp: 彼[かれ]は話[はなし]が上手[じょうず]で、相手[あいて]から本音[ほんね]を{引[ひ]き出[だ]す|cv-dasu}のがうまい。
en: He is a good talker and is skilled at drawing out people's true feelings.
why: Getting the truth out of someone is 引き出す; 引き受ける means to take on a task.

jp: 先生[せんせい]は封筒[ふうとう]から試験[しけん]の紙[かみ]を{取[と]り出[だ]した|cv-dasu}。
en: The teacher took the exam papers out of the envelope.
why: The papers come out of the envelope (から), so 取り出す; 取り消す means to cancel.

jp: 彼[かれ]は笑顔[えがお]で右手[みぎて]を{差[さ]し出[だ]した|cv-dasu}。
en: He held out his right hand with a smile.
why: 差し出す is to hold something out toward someone; 差し込む is to insert and 差し引く to deduct.

jp: 「行[い]こう」と言[い]って、父[ちち]は先[さき]に{歩[ある]き出[だ]した|cv-dasu}。
en: "Let's go," said my father, and he started walking ahead.
why: Saying "let's go" and then setting off is 歩き出す, the start of walking.

jp: 駅[えき]の前[まえ]で、酔[よ]った男[おとこ]の人[ひと]が急[きゅう]に{歌[うた]い出[だ]した|cv-dasu}。
en: In front of the station, a drunk man suddenly started to sing.
why: 急に marks a sudden beginning, which is the meaning of 歌い出す.

jp: 春[はる]になって、庭[にわ]の花[はな]が一斉[いっせい]に{咲[さ]き出[だ]した|cv-dasu}。
en: Spring came, and the flowers in the garden all started to bloom at once.
why: As spring arrives the flowers begin to open, so 咲き出す (start blooming) fits.

jp: 社長[しゃちょう]は上着[うわぎ]のポケットから名刺[めいし]を{取[と]り出[だ]した|cv-dasu}。
en: The company president took a business card out of a jacket pocket.
why: から names the pocket as the source, so 取り出す (take out) is the verb.

jp: 百枚[ひゃくまい]の写真[しゃしん]の中[なか]から、一番[いちばん]いい一枚[いちまい]を{選[えら]び出[だ]した|cv-dasu}。
en: I picked out the best one from a hundred photos.
why: 選び出す is to pick one out from a larger group, which is what 中から (from among) sets up.
